title: Chorizo Breakfast Tacos
subtitle: Spicy chorizo, warm tortillas
description: Spicy chorizo, warm tortillas. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Mix batter gently
steps.instruction: Whisk dry and wet separately; combine until just mixed. Lumps are fine — over-mixing makes tough pancakes.

steps.title: Bake bacon, hold oven
steps.instruction: Bake bacon at 400°F on sheet pans 15–18 minutes until crisp. Set oven to 200°F to hold finished pancakes and eggs.

steps.title: Griddle in batches
steps.instruction: Griddle at 375°F: pancakes 2–3 minutes per side until golden; eggs if serving scrambled in batches. Common mistake: heat too high — outside burns before center sets.

steps.title: Serve the line
steps.instruction: Chorizo Breakfast Tacos does not wait — call the crew as batches finish. Syrup and butter on the table; backup tray in the 200°F oven.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Warm tortillas in a dry skillet stack — wrap in foil so the line stays soft.
Set proteins, salsa, and toppings in separate bowls for build-your-own station flow.
Keep hot items on one side of the table and cold on the other — eggs stay hot, fruit stays cold.
Line up Chorizo Breakfast Tacos on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Spicy chorizo, warm tortillas. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
